note: 8 past exams, 2010–2023. Part A = 6 computational problems (5 credits each, need 15 to pass); Part B/C = theory proofs. The professor recycles ~8 problem templates every year — see study-guide/professor-exam-playbook.md.

templates.T3: Integration technique (substitution / by parts / partial fractions)
templates.T5: Recursive sequence — show the limit exists, then compute it
templates.T7: Radius of convergence of a power series

problems.statement: Compute lim_(x->0) (e^(x^2/2) - cos x - x^2)/(x sin x - x^2).
Compute integral x^2 sqrt(x^2-4) dx.
problems.solution: Trig substitution x=2 sec t, sqrt(x^2-4)=2 tan t, dx=2 sec t tan t dt gives 16 integral (sec^5 t - sec^3 t) dt. Reduce sec powers, back-substitute: (x(x^2-2)sqrt(x^2-4))/4 - 2 ln|x+sqrt(x^2-4)| + C.

problems.statement: Is the integral integral_1^infinity (1/sqrt(x)) sin(1/x) dx convergent or divergent?
problems.solution: For x>=1, 0<sin(1/x)<=1/x, so 0 < (1/sqrt(x))sin(1/x) <= 1/x^(3/2). Since integral_1^infinity dx/x^(3/2) converges (p=3/2>1), the comparison test gives convergence.

problems.statement: Let a_0=12 and a_(n+1)=sqrt(7 a_n - 3) - 1 for n>=0. Show that lim_(n->infinity) a_n exists and compute it.
problems.solution: By induction a_n is bounded below by 4 and decreasing, so the limit L exists. Passing to the limit: L=sqrt(7L-3)-1 gives L^2+2L+1=7L-3, i.e. L^2-5L+4=0, so L=1 or 4; since a_n>=4, L=4.

problems.statement: Determine convergence: a) sum_(n=1)^inf (1-1/n^2)   b) sum_(n=2)^inf n·sin(1/n^3)   c) sum_(n=1)^inf 2^n (1-1/n^2)^(n^3).
problems.answer: a) Divergent  b) Convergent  c) Convergent
problems.solution: a) term -> 1 != 0, diverges (nth-term test). b) n sin(1/n^3) ~ n·(1/n^3)=1/n^2, limit comparison with sum 1/n^2 -> converges. c) root test: (2^n(1-1/n^2)^(n^3))^(1/n)=2(1-1/n^2)^(n^2) -> 2e^(-1) < 1, converges.

problems.statement: For the series sum_(n=2)^inf (-1)^n/(n·(ln n)^r): a) for which r does it converge?  b) for which r is it absolutely convergent?
problems.solution: a) Terms 1/(n(ln n)^r) decrease to 0 for every real r (eventually), so by the Alternating Series Test it converges for all r. b) |term|=1/(n(ln n)^r); by the integral test integral dx/(x(ln x)^r) converges iff r>1, so absolutely convergent exactly for r>1.

problems.statement: Define 'bounded from above/below' and define the supremum and infimum of a bounded set.
problems.solution: S is bounded above if there is M with x<=M for all x in S (M an upper bound); bounded below similarly. sup S = the least upper bound; inf S = the greatest lower bound.

problems.statement: Given lim_(x->a) f(x)=A and lim_(x->a) g(x)=B, prove lim_(x->a) f(x)g(x)=AB.
problems.solution: Write fg-AB = f(g-B)+B(f-A). Given eps>0, choose delta so |f-A|, |g-B| are small; f is bounded near a (|f|<=|A|+1). Then |fg-AB| <= |f||g-B|+|B||f-A| < eps. ★ Highest-frequency proof on this exam — memorize it.

problems.statement: Define an absolutely convergent series and prove that if sum a_n is absolutely convergent then it converges.
problems.solution: 0 <= a_n+|a_n| <= 2|a_n|; since sum 2|a_n| converges, by comparison sum (a_n+|a_n|) converges; then sum a_n = sum(a_n+|a_n|) - sum|a_n| converges as a difference of convergent series.

problems.statement: Compute lim_(x->0) ((1+x^2)^(1/2) - cos x - x^2)/(x arctan x - x^2).
Determine integral cos^3(5x)·sin^2(2x) dx.
problems.answer: A sum of sine terms (see method)
problems.solution: Use cos^3(5x)=cos(5x)(1-sin^2 5x) or product-to-sum repeatedly to turn the product into a sum of cos/sin of multiple angles, then integrate term by term. Result is a linear combination of sin(19x), sin(15x), sin(11x), sin(9x), sin(5x), sin(x).

problems.statement: Is integral_2^infinity (sqrt(x+1) - sqrt(x-1))·arctan(1/x) dx convergent or divergent?
problems.solution: sqrt(x+1)-sqrt(x-1)=2/(sqrt(x+1)+sqrt(x-1)) ~ 1/sqrt(x); arctan(1/x) ~ 1/x. Product ~ 1/x^(3/2), so by (limit) comparison with the convergent p=3/2 integral it converges.

problems.statement: Determine the radius of convergence: a) sum ((n+1)!-(n-1)!)/n! x^n   b) sum 2^n(1-1/n^2)^(n^3) x^n.
Determine convergence: a) sum cos(1/n^2)   b) sum_(n=2) 1/(n ln n)   c) sum (2n)^n n!/n^(2n).
problems.answer: a) Divergent  b) Divergent  c) Convergent
problems.solution: a) term -> 1 != 0. b) integral test: integral dx/(x ln x)=ln(ln x) -> infinity, diverges. c) ratio test gives limit 2/e < 1 (using n!~(n/e)^n), converges.

problems.statement: Let f be differentiable near 0 with f(0)=0 and f'(x)=x^2+(f(x))^2. Compute lim_(x->0) f(x)/x^3. (Hint: differentiate the equation.)
Show that there are infinitely many primes.
problems.solution: Suppose finitely many p_1..p_k. N=p_1...p_k+1 has a prime factor, which cannot be any p_i (they leave remainder 1), contradiction.

problems.statement: Prove the factor theorem: p(alpha)=0 iff (x-alpha) divides p(x).
problems.solution: Divide: p(x)=(x-alpha)q(x)+r with r constant. Then p(alpha)=r. So p(alpha)=0 iff r=0 iff (x-alpha)|p(x).

problems.statement: Prove that cos(s-t)=cos s cos t + sin s sin t.
problems.solution: Standard: use the unit-circle dot product of (cos s, sin s) and (cos t, sin t), or Euler's formula e^(i(s-t)) and take real parts.

problems.statement: Compute lim_(x->0) (e^x - cos x - sin x - x^2 - x^3/3)/(x^2(1-cos(x^2))).
problems.solution: e^x-cos x-sin x = x^2 + x^3/3 + x^6/360 + ...; subtracting x^2+x^3/3 leaves x^6/360+O(x^7). Denominator x^2(1-cos x^2)=x^2·x^4/2=x^6/2. Ratio -> (1/360)/(1/2)=1/180.

problems.statement: Is integral_1^infinity (1 - cos(1/x)) dx convergent or divergent?
problems.solution: 1-cos(1/x) ~ (1/2)(1/x)^2 = 1/(2x^2) as x->infinity. Limit comparison with sum/integral of 1/x^2 (p=2>1) gives convergence.

problems.statement: Compute integral (2x^3+5x^2+6x-2)/((x+1)^2(4+x^2)) dx.
problems.answer: a ln|x+1| + b/(x+1) + c ln(x^2+4) + d arctan(x/2) + C

problems.statement: Let a_0=6 and a_(n+1)=sqrt(2 a_n - 3) + 2. Show the limit exists and compute it.
problems.solution: a_n is decreasing and bounded below (a_1=5, a_2=sqrt(7)+2≈4.65,...), so L exists. L=sqrt(2L-3)+2 gives (L-2)^2=2L-3, L^2-6L+7=0, L=3±sqrt(2); since a_n>3, L=3+sqrt(2).

problems.statement: Determine convergence: a) sum e^(1/n^2)   b) sum n·tan(1/n^2)   c) sum 2^(-n)(1+1/n)^(n^2).
problems.answer: a) Divergent  b) Divergent  c) Divergent
problems.solution: a) term -> 1 != 0. b) n tan(1/n^2) ~ n·1/n^2 = 1/n, diverges (limit comparison). c) root test: (2^(-n)(1+1/n)^(n^2))^(1/n)=(1/2)(1+1/n)^n -> e/2 > 1, diverges.

problems.statement: Determine the convergence of sum_(n=2)^inf 1/(n·ln n·(ln ln n)^2).
problems.solution: Integral test with u=ln(ln x): integral dx/(x ln x (ln ln x)^2) = integral du/u^2 = -1/u, which converges. Hence the series converges.

problems.statement: For s=sum_(n=0)^inf x^n: show a) it converges to 1/(1-x) for |x|<1, b) it diverges otherwise.
problems.solution: Partial sum s_N=(1-x^(N+1))/(1-x) for x!=1. If |x|<1, x^(N+1)->0 so s_N->1/(1-x). If |x|>=1 the terms do not tend to 0, so it diverges.

problems.statement: Prove the first part of the root test: if a_n>0 and M=lim a_n^(1/n) exists with 0<=M<1, then sum a_n converges.
problems.solution: Pick r with M<r<1. For large n, a_n^(1/n)<r so a_n<r^n; sum r^n converges (geometric), so by comparison sum a_n converges.

problems.statement: Prove the uniqueness of Taylor expansions (a_n=b_n and R_N=Q_N).
problems.solution: Subtract the two expansions: sum(a_n-b_n)(x-a)^n = Q_N-R_N. Dividing by (x-a)^k and letting x->a successively forces a_0=b_0, a_1=b_1, ..., hence all a_n=b_n and R_N=Q_N.

problems.statement: Compute lim_(x->0) (1 - cos(x^2))/(x(ln(1+x) + e^(-x) - 1)).
Evaluate integral cos(3x)·sin^4(2x) dx.
problems.solution: Write sin^4(2x)=((1-cos 4x)/2)^2 and expand, or use product-to-sum on cos(3x)sin^4(2x); integrate the resulting sum of sines/cosines of multiple angles term by term.

problems.statement: Compute integral 1/(1 + sqrt(x^2+1)) dx.
problems.solution: Rationalize: multiply by (sqrt(x^2+1)-1)/(sqrt(x^2+1)-1) to get (sqrt(x^2+1)-1)/x^2. Then integral sqrt(x^2+1)/x^2 dx - integral 1/x^2 dx = [-sqrt(x^2+1)/x + ln|x+sqrt(x^2+1)|] + 1/x.

problems.statement: Determine convergence: a) sum e^(-1/n)   b) sum sqrt(n)·tan(1/n^2)   c) sum 7^(-n) C(3n,2n).
problems.answer: a) Divergent  b) Convergent  c) Convergent
problems.solution: a) term -> 1 != 0. b) sqrt(n)tan(1/n^2) ~ sqrt(n)/n^2 = 1/n^(3/2), converges. c) ratio test on 7^(-n)C(3n,2n): the binomial ratio -> 27/4, times 1/7 -> 27/28 < 1, converges.

problems.statement: Is integral_2^infinity tan(1/(x sqrt(x)))/(sqrt(x^2+1) - sqrt(x^2-1)) dx convergent or divergent? (leading-order comparison)
problems.solution: sqrt(x^2+1)-sqrt(x^2-1)=2/(sqrt(x^2+1)+sqrt(x^2-1)) ~ 1/x, so 1/(that) ~ x; the tan factor ~ 1/(x sqrt x). Product ~ x·1/(x sqrt x)=1/sqrt(x), and integral 1/sqrt(x) (p=1/2) diverges. (Check the exact grouping on the paper; method is leading-order comparison.)

problems.statement: Determine the convergence of sum 2^(n^2)/n^n·(1-1/n^3)^(n^5).
problems.solution: Root test: (2^(n^2)/n^n)^(1/n)=2^n/n -> infinity, while (1-1/n^3)^(n^4) -> 1. Limit is infinity > 1, so it diverges.

problems.statement: Prove lim_(x->a) f(x)g(x) = A·B given the individual limits A, B.
problems.solution: fg-AB=f(g-B)+B(f-A); f is bounded near a; make each piece < eps/2. ★ Same must-know proof.

problems.statement: Prove the ratio test: a_n>0, M=lim a_(n+1)/a_n; converges if 0<=M<1, diverges if M>1.
problems.solution: M<1: pick r in (M,1); for large n a_(n+1)<r a_n so a_n<=C r^n, compare with geometric. M>1: terms increase, do not tend to 0, diverges.

problems.statement: Prove the integral test: for f decreasing, non-negative, sum f(n) converges iff integral_1^infinity f converges.
problems.solution: Since f decreases, integral_n^(n+1) f <= f(n) <= integral_(n-1)^n f. Summing bounds the partial sums between tails of the integral, so series and integral converge together.

problems.statement: Compute lim_(x->0) (ln(1+x) + arctan x - 2x + x^2/2)/(x - sin x).
problems.solution: ln(1+x)+arctan x = 2x - x^2/2 + 0·x^3 - x^4/4 + ...; subtracting 2x - x^2/2 leaves -x^4/4+O(x^5). Denominator x-sin x = x^3/6. Ratio ~ (-x^4/4)/(x^3/6) = -3x/2 -> 0.

problems.statement: Evaluate integral cos^2(2x)·sin^3(3x) dx.
problems.solution: cos^2(2x)=(1+cos 4x)/2 and sin^3(3x)=sin(3x)(1-cos^2 3x); expand the product with product-to-sum identities and integrate term by term.

problems.statement: Compute integral sqrt(x^2-1)/x dx.
problems.solution: Substitute x=sec t, sqrt(x^2-1)=tan t, dx=sec t tan t dt: integral tan^2 t dt = integral(sec^2 t -1)dt = tan t - t. Back-substitute: sqrt(x^2-1) - arccos(1/x) + C.

problems.statement: Determine convergence: a) sum tan(1/n^2)   b) sum 1/(n cos(1/n^2))   c) sum C(3n,n)C(4n,n)/C(5n,2n).
problems.answer: a) Convergent  b) Divergent  c) (ratio test)
problems.solution: a) tan(1/n^2)~1/n^2, converges. b) 1/(n cos(1/n^2))~1/n, diverges. c) ratio test on the binomial expression: compute the limit of consecutive-term ratio and compare to 1.

problems.statement: Determine the convergence of integral_1^infinity tan(1/x)·1/(1+(ln x)^2) dx. (Hint: compare with g(x)=1/(x(1+(ln x)^2)).)
problems.solution: tan(1/x) ~ 1/x, so the integrand ~ g(x)=1/(x(1+(ln x)^2)). With u=ln x, integral g = integral du/(1+u^2)=arctan(ln x), which converges. Limit comparison gives convergence.

problems.statement: Determine the convergence of sum ((n^3+n)^(1/3) - n).
problems.solution: (n^3+n)^(1/3)=n(1+1/n^2)^(1/3)=n + 1/(3n) + O(1/n^3), so the term ~ 1/(3n). By limit comparison with sum 1/n it diverges.

problems.statement: Prove lim_(x->a) f(x)/g(x) = A/B (with B != 0).
problems.solution: Show 1/g -> 1/B (using |g|>=|B|/2 near a), then combine with the product law. ★ Second must-know proof.

problems.statement: Prove the root test (converges for 0<=M<1).
problems.solution: Pick r in (M,1); eventually a_n^(1/n)<r so a_n<r^n; compare with the convergent geometric series.

problems.statement: State/prove a comparison or convergence result as posed on the paper.
problems.solution: Follow the standard comparison-test argument (bound terms by a known convergent/divergent series).

problems.statement: Compute integral x^2 ln(x) dx.
problems.solution: Integration by parts with u=ln x, dv=x^2 dx: = (x^3/3)ln x - integral (x^3/3)(1/x) dx = (x^3/3)ln x - x^3/9 + C.

problems.statement: Compute lim_(x->0) (arctan x - x e^(-x^2/3))/(x^3 - x^2 sin x).
Determine convergence: a) sum cos(1/n^3)   b) sum n^2·sin(1/n^3)   c) sum (n!)^4/2^(n^2).
problems.answer: a) Divergent  b) Divergent  c) Convergent
problems.solution: a) term -> 1 != 0. b) n^2 sin(1/n^3) ~ n^2/n^3 = 1/n, diverges. c) ratio test: a_(n+1)/a_n = (n+1)^4/2^(2n+1) -> 0 < 1, converges.

problems.statement: Evaluate integral cos^2(4x)·sin^4(2x) dx.
problems.solution: Use cos^2(4x)=(1+cos 8x)/2 and sin^4(2x)=((1-cos 4x)/2)^2; multiply out, apply product-to-sum to the cross terms, and integrate the resulting cosines term by term.

problems.statement: Determine the convergence of integral_0^infinity ((1+x)/(1+x^2) - e^(-1/x)) dx.
problems.solution: Split at 1. Near x->infinity expand (1+x)/(1+x^2) and e^(-1/x) to compare leading 1/x powers; near x->0 check the (possibly improper) behaviour of e^(-1/x) -> 0. Convergence is decided by the leading-order comparison at each end.

problems.statement: a) Show lim_(x->infinity) a x^alpha / x^r = 0 (suitable a, alpha, r). b) Generalized root test with a_n^(1/n^alpha)=M. c) Use b) for sum (1-1/n)^(n^(6/5)).
problems.solution: c) (1-1/n)^(n^(6/5)) = exp(n^(6/5) ln(1-1/n)) ~ exp(-n^(1/5)) -> 0 faster than any power, so the series converges (by the generalized root test in b).

problems.statement: Prove Taylor's formula at x=a: f(x)=sum_(k=0)^(N-1) f^(k)(a)(x-a)^k/k! + remainder, for some theta between a and x.
problems.solution: Apply repeated integration by parts to the integral form of the remainder, or use the generalized Mean Value Theorem (Cauchy) to get the Lagrange remainder f^(N)(theta)(x-a)^N/N!.

problems.statement: Compute integral 1/(2 cos x - 3 sin x + 3) dx.
problems.solution: With t=tan(x/2): cos x=(1-t^2)/(1+t^2), sin x=2t/(1+t^2), dx=2 dt/(1+t^2). The integrand becomes a rational function of t; integrate (partial fractions) and substitute back t=tan(x/2).

problems.statement: Compute lim_(x->0) (arctan x - x(1-x^2)^(1/3))/(x^3 - x ln(1+x^2)).
Determine the radius of convergence: a) sum n^2 x^n   b) sum 3^(-n)·2^n·... x^n   c) sum 3^n x^n/2^(n^2).
problems.solution: a) |a_n|^(1/n)=(n^2)^(1/n) -> 1, R=1. c) a_n=3^n/2^(n^2), a_n^(1/n)=3/2^n -> 0, so R=infinity. (b) apply root/ratio to the given coefficient similarly.)

problems.statement: Find the general solution of y'' + 4y' + 5y = e^(-2x) x sin x.
problems.answer: Resonant case (roots -2 ± i match the forcing)
problems.solution: Homogeneous roots: r^2+4r+5=0 -> r=-2±i, so y_h=e^(-2x)(C1 cos x + C2 sin x). The forcing e^(-2x)x sin x resonates with these roots, so try y_p=e^(-2x)·x·[(ax+b)cos x + (cx+d)sin x]; substitute and match coefficients.

problems.statement: Determine the convergence of integral_1^infinity sqrt(x+1)(1 - e^(-1/x^2)) dx.
problems.solution: 1 - e^(-1/x^2) ~ 1/x^2 and sqrt(x+1) ~ sqrt(x), so the integrand ~ sqrt(x)/x^2 = 1/x^(3/2). Limit comparison with the convergent p=3/2 integral gives convergence.

problems.statement: Show that lim_(n->infinity) ( sum_(k=1)^n 1/k - ln n ) exists.
problems.solution: Let x_n = sum_(k=1)^n 1/k - ln n. Show x_n is decreasing (x_(n+1)-x_n = 1/(n+1) - ln(1+1/n) < 0) and bounded below by 0 (since 1/k >= integral_k^(k+1) dx/x). A decreasing sequence bounded below converges.

problems.statement: Prove lim_(x->a) f(x)g(x) = A·B.
problems.solution: fg-AB=f(g-B)+B(f-A); bound and make small.

problems.statement: With B != 0, prove lim_(x->a) f(x)/g(x) = A/B.
problems.solution: Show 1/g -> 1/B, then apply the product law.

problems.statement: Prove the uniqueness of Taylor expansions.
problems.solution: Subtract the two expansions and let x->a repeatedly to force equal coefficients.

problems.statement: Compute integral 1/(2 cos x + 3 sin x + 3) dx.
problems.solution: t=tan(x/2) gives cos x=(1-t^2)/(1+t^2), sin x=2t/(1+t^2), dx=2dt/(1+t^2); reduces to a rational integral in t, then back-substitute.

problems.statement: Compute lim_(x->0) (arctan x - x(1-x^2)^(1/3))/(x^4 - x^3 ln(1+x)).
Determine the radius of convergence: a) sum n^5 x^n   b) sum (n!)^5·2^(-n^2) x^n   c) sum (1-1/n^2)^(n^3) x^n.
problems.answer: a) R=1  b) R=infinity  c) R=e

problems.statement: Find the general solution of y'' - 4y' + 5y = e^(2x) x sin x.
problems.answer: Resonant case (roots 2 ± i match the forcing)
problems.solution: Roots r^2-4r+5=0 -> 2±i, y_h=e^(2x)(C1 cos x+C2 sin x). Resonance: y_p=e^(2x)·x·[(ax+b)cos x+(cx+d)sin x]; substitute and match.

problems.statement: Determine the convergence of integral_0^infinity ((x^3+1)/x^3)^(1/4)(1 - e^(-1/x^2)) dx.
problems.solution: As x->infinity: ((x^3+1)/x^3)^(1/4) -> 1 and 1-e^(-1/x^2) ~ 1/x^2, so the tail ~ 1/x^2 (converges). Near x->0 check ((x^3+1)/x^3)^(1/4) ~ x^(-3/4) against 1-e^(-1/x^2) -> 1; the small-x behaviour ~ x^(-3/4) (p=3/4<1) integrates finitely. Both ends converge.

problems.statement: Find a so that lim_(x->infinity) [ x^(3/2)(x+1)^(1/2) + x^(5/3)(x+1)^(1/3) - 2 x^(7/4)(x+1)^(1/4) + x^2 ln x - x^2 ln(a+x) ] is finite; find the limit.
problems.answer: a chosen to cancel the x^2·(a/x)=a x term; then evaluate
problems.solution: Expand each (x+1)^p = x^p(1+1/x)^p = x^p(1+p/x+...) and ln(a+x)=ln x + a/x - a^2/(2x^2)+.... Collect powers of x: cancel the divergent x^2 and x terms by choosing a appropriately, then read off the finite constant limit from the remaining O(1) term.

problems.statement: Prove lim_(x->a) f(x)g(x) = A·B.
problems.solution: fg-AB=f(g-B)+B(f-A); bound and make small.

problems.statement: With B != 0, prove lim_(x->a) f(x)/g(x) = A/B.
problems.solution: Show 1/g -> 1/B, then apply the product law.

problems.statement: Prove the uniqueness of Taylor expansions.
problems.solution: Subtract expansions and let x->a repeatedly.
